title: Closed-test chain mate and the normalized derived restriction
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and on every small pro-etale site put $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use internal $\Lambda_Y$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], their exact inverse images and ordinary unbounded derived direct images computed on K-injectives [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. All sites and section values are taken in a common sufficiently large universe. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak a\subseteq A$ an ideal, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $s:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak a)\hookrightarrow U$. Let $v$ be the affine ind-etale closed-site lift [def-exc-closed-site-lift]. Let $V\to Z$ be an affine ind-etale object such that $V$ and $B=v(V)$ are w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Let $f:X\to U$ be a morphism of affine schemes and put $X_Z=X\times_UZ$, with projections $h:X_Z\to X$, $f_Z:X_Z\to Z$. Put $T=X\times_UB$, $T_0=X\times_UV$ and $a:T_0\hookrightarrow T$; products mean scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $\eta_b,\varepsilon_b$ for the specified unit and counit of $b^*\dashv b_*$, and $\theta:f_Z^*s^*\cong h^*f^*$ for canonical pullback composition. Define
$$\operatorname{Ex}^0_F=(f_Z)_*(h^*\varepsilon_{f,F}\circ\theta_{f_*F})\circ\eta_{f_Z,s^*f_*F}:s^*f_*F\to(f_Z)_*h^*F$$
[def-weil-pbc-adjunction-square-exchange]. Under the inverse of the actual closed unit-section isomorphism $(f_*F)(B)\to(s^*f_*F)(V)$ and the direct-image section formulas, $\operatorname{Ex}^0_F(V)$ is precisely
$$F(T)\xrightarrow{\eta_{a,F|_T}(T)}(a^*(F|_T))(T_0)=(h^*F)(T_0).$$
Let $\mathcal I$ be a K-injective representative of a bounded-below $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$, let $j:h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ be a K-injective resolution, and set $e=(f_Z)_*j\circ\operatorname{Ex}^0_{\mathcal I}$. In the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], $Q(e)$ represents the derived exchange whose adjunct under $f_Z^*\dashv R(f_Z)_*$ is $h^*\varepsilon_f\circ\theta$. Its evaluation, with the actual closed unit and localized section identities, is
$$Q\bigl(\mathcal I(T)\xrightarrow{\eta_a}(h^*\mathcal I)(T_0)\xrightarrow{j(T_0)}\mathcal J(T_0)\bigr).$$
Under the canonical K-injective section-localization identifications this arrow is the derived unit for $a^*\dashv Ra_*$ followed by $R\Gamma(T,Ra_*(-))\cong R\Gamma(T_0,-)$. The latter composition is normalized by $\Gamma(T,a_*\mathcal J|_{T_0})=\Gamma(T_0,\mathcal J|_{T_0})$ degreewise. The localized adjunctions and the derived composition comparisons preserve the specified units and counits. Neither exchange nor restriction is asserted invertible.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-closed-test-unit-evaluation] to pass to section-ring modules, preserving the specified inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions. In particular $(f_*F)(B)=F(T)$ and $((f_Z)_*h^*F)(V)=(h^*F)(T_0)$. The source identification is $u^{-1}$, where $u:(f_*F)(B)\to(s^*f_*F)(V)$ is the actual unit section and is invertible. Thus it suffices to calculate $\operatorname{Ex}^0_F(V)u(x)$ for $x\in F(T)$; no inverse of exchange is used.

source.place: Tag 09BL, lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply (1)–(2); actual unit normalization supplied by the cited node.

proof.text: Expand the specified square mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-square-exchange]. By [def-sfb-proetale-inverse-image-unit-section], unit insertion first gives $f_Z^{-1}(s^{-1}x)$ on $T_0$. The geometric pullback composition [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] identifies this with $h^{-1}(f^{-1}x)$, with the canonical fibre-product pasting. For clarity, the counit here has a concrete description: in the inverse-image colimit [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], a generator $(W,\phi:L\to X\times_UW,y\in F(X\times_UW))$ is sent by $\varepsilon_f$ to $F(\phi)y$. Indeed these maps form the adjunct of the identity of $f_*F$. For $W=B$, $L=T$, $\phi=1_T$, the value is $x$. After $h^{-1}$ and restriction to $T_0$ it is therefore the inverse-image unit section of $x$ for $a:T_0\to T$. This proves $\operatorname{Ex}^0_F(V)u(x)=\eta_{a,F|_T}(T)(x)$. The coefficient isomorphisms from the point are the ones in the specified module adjunction, so the calculation is linear, not just set-valued.

proof.text: For closed_test_localized_adjunctions, first prove the conjugacy identities for any commutative square, without localization hypotheses. Conjugation reverses transitivity and preserves inverses. Apply CondensedRing.conjugateIsoEquiv_upperStarComp to the two ordinary compositors in [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]; equality induction identifies the conjugate of the middle equality transport. This gives directSquare as the conjugate of ordinarySquare. For right-derived composition use the source-library theorem Adjunction.rightDerivedFunctorCompIso'_hom_eq_conjugateEquiv on the specified ordinary adjunctions. Right derivation preserves composition of natural isomorphisms; equality induction again treats the middle transport, yielding derivedDirectSquare as the conjugate of square. Expanding the exact localization compositors identifies square with Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso ordinarySquare, hence the test comparison is derivedTestPullbackComposition. These are the actual constructions of [def-sfb-closed-test-derived-exchange-maps] and [def-sfb-closed-test-kinjective-section-maps]. Specialize to the test square and to each of the last three displayed squares. Every helper in this calculation is proved in Lean. No localized-model coherence theorem or separate derived-composition normalization theorem is needed for this clause.

It is correct and acceptable as elementary. Step 3 gives the transpose (f_Z)_*j∘Ex^0=e, and the derived counit Q(ε_I) via the resolving-adjunction node, whose hypotheses hold because f_Z^* is exact. Step 5: I_T and J_0 are K-injective through the section-ring equivalence, j_0 is a quasi-isomorphism, and the derived unit is the class of a_*j_0∘η_a; it never claims a^*I_T is K-injective. Step 6: a_*J_0 is K-injective because a^* is an exact left adjoint, and the ringed-topos composition with an identity resolution gives Γ(T,a_*J_0)=J(T_0). Step 7 takes the localized unit/counit coherence from the statements of the sibling node and the generic composition node. Edge cases checked: ideal 0, ideal A (empty T_0), f=id, K=0. I accept the five declared generic tool_uses.
